title: Spec-driven changes with OpenSpec
summary: The convention for keeping current behaviour in openspec/specs/ and work in flight in openspec/changes/ (propose, apply, sync, archive), plus a guard that validates them. The OpenSpec CLI generates its own commands and skills.
postInstall: Install the OpenSpec CLI at a pinned version (the convention was written against @fission-ai/openspec 1.10.0) and run `openspec init --tools claude` in the project: the non-interactive form.

Read docs/conventions/openspec-workflow.md § What the generated files pre-approve before committing what it generates: each generated file lets a session run any `openspec` subcommand without a prompt, `feedback` (a public issue, through gh) and `config` included.

Commit what it generates — six commands under .claude/commands/opsx/ (propose, explore, apply, update, sync, archive) and six skills under .claude/skills/openspec-* — and never hand-edit those files: `openspec update` rewrites them after a CLI upgrade, `openspec update --force` at any time.
A change with no delta (tooling, documentation) declares `skip_specs: true` in its .openspec.yaml: without it, `openspec validate` and so OS-1 reject the change.
Close a change in two steps, sync then archive: archiving alone can leave its deltas out of the specs (docs/conventions/openspec-workflow.md).

With the agents module, the verifier validates the OpenSpec files by running the gate, where OS-1 turns the CLI's telemetry off. Do not list the bare `openspec validate` in .claude/hooks/agent-bash-guard.config.json: it reports to the CLI's telemetry, and the guard's environment prefixes include neither switch that turns it off.
